comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Reconciliation for sibling ambery-candied-binturong (push race in this same fixture family), from the depraved-frowzy-trout 23-site audit.

The failing site is NEITHER in trout's converted set NOR in its deliberately-kept set — it is a third category the audit did not cover.

- The failure is `_git("push", "-q", "origin", "HEAD:tickets", cwd=tracker_a)` inside `_assert_emit_is_append_only`, old line 1714, now line 1738 after the trout change shifted the file.
- Trout's scope was strictly the 23 `_expire_sync_marker` + `_engine_run(...)` READ-side sync pairs. Raw `_git("push", ...)` legs are a separate category — 18 of them in this file — neither converted nor classified.
- The trout commit's hunks never enter `_assert_emit_is_append_only`'s body (verified with `git show 4f36783f24 --unified=0`). The only interaction: the `_sync_from_origin` definition MOVED from old line 1680 up to line 95, above that function, which still calls it unchanged (now line 1749).

Why it is outside carp's and trout's failure mode by construction: that push is already `check=True`, i.e. fail-fast. It is NOT a sync-by-side-effect — it raises CalledProcessError loudly rather than silently failing to establish a precondition, which is why this manifests as a hard error rather than the 'clones do not share a base' signature. So the trout change neither fixes nor masks it, and converting read-sync sites could not have.

Practical steer: the lead already in this ticket's description is the better one — base cc69cc1179 changed the tickets-store write-lock RETRY, and a push leg racing two clones at one remote is exactly the subsystem that touches. The push legs, not the read-sync legs, are the unexamined surface.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
ROOT CAUSE — the filed premise (a lost CAS / non-fast-forward between the two clones) is
falsified by the job's own captured log.

The push was rejected by the RECEIVING repository, not by a ref race. The log carries
`unresolved deltas left after unpacking`, `remote unpack failed: unpack-objects abnormal
exit`, and `refs/heads/tickets does not point to a valid object!`. A sweep of the recent CI
history found no `non-fast-forward`, no `cannot lock ref`, and no OOM/signal in that job.
The warning repeats 18 times with a monotonically climbing unpushed-commit counter, so the
bare `remote.git` was already missing objects from the FIRST emit push: the remote was
corrupt before any invariant assertion ran.

Cross-check against the sibling occurrence recorded on chewed-illicit-blacklemur: that one
failed with clone B holding an EMPTY event set and a clean git log, with no push warnings at
all. Different mechanism, already fixed by willing-cellular-carp. The corruption signature
appears exactly once in the swept history, which is consistent with a rare race rather than
a deterministic defect.

MECHANISM. Three facts compose:

1. `two_clones` creates the bare remote with a plain `git init --bare` and never configures
   it.
2. `_make_repo` clones that local path without `--no-hardlinks`, so git's local optimization
   HARDLINKS the remote's object files into each clone. Measured, not assumed: an assertion
   over `(st_dev, st_ino)` pairs showed clone B sharing 19 object files with the remote.
   `.tickets-tracker` is a linked worktree, so it shares its clone's object database.
3. rebar's gc-config ensure unit keeps auto-gc enabled but forces it FOREGROUND
   (`gc.autoDetach=false`, `maintenance.autoDetach=false`) exactly because a DETACHED
   background gc/maintenance repacks an object database outside the write lock and corrupts
   the store — bug 88eb, ADR 0051, recorded in the `rebar._store.sync` module docstring.

That pinning reaches every repository rebar owns. It does not reach a bare remote, which
rebar does not own. So the harness's `remote.git` was the one repository in the fixture whose
`receive-pack` ran `git gc --auto` at git's defaults — detached — after each of the ~50 emit
pushes, rewriting the object store the next push depended on. git-clone(1) separately warns
that the hardlink mode can race with concurrent modification of the source repository.

Two operations interleave, and both are on the REMOTE rather than between the clones: the
detached upkeep process spawned by push N, and the object transfer of push N+1.

WHY IT IS NOT LOCALLY REPRODUCIBLE. Confirmed: the file passes standalone and under CI's
`-n 4 --dist loadgroup`. Forcing `gc.auto=1` on the remote made gc run (108 loose objects
repacked) but did not corrupt it on this host, which is expected for a timing race that
needed one specific interleaving on one ubuntu-24.04 runner.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
FIX + VERIFICATION (Gerrit change 1676).

The fix is at the two fixture sites that own the remote's storage, which covers all 16
`push … HEAD:tickets` sites in the file at once:

- `_init_bare_remote` creates the bare remote and pins `gc.autoDetach=false`,
  `maintenance.autoDetach=false` (the posture rebar guarantees on every tracker it owns) plus
  `receive.autogc=false`, so a push can never trigger a concurrent rewrite of the object
  store the NEXT push depends on. A throwaway fixture remote has no reason to run upkeep.
- `_make_repo` clones with `--no-hardlinks`, so the remote's, clone A's and clone B's object
  stores are independent and the only thing crossing between them is what a push or fetch
  actually transfers — which is what these tests characterize.

AC3 (no masking) is satisfied by construction: the change removes a concurrent mutator. It
adds no retry, no swallowed error, no relaxed assertion and no timing bound, and every setup
push stays `check=True`. `test_setup_push_still_fails_when_the_push_genuinely_cannot_succeed`
pins that directly: clone B publishes a commit, clone A commits offline, and A's push is then
a true non-fast-forward that must still raise `CalledProcessError`.

AC2: `test_fixture_remote_runs_no_detached_upkeep_and_shares_no_objects` asserts the posture
and the object-store independence, converting a rare CI-only corruption into a deterministic
local oracle. RED verified for BOTH limbs against a working copy with the fix removed:

- pins removed -> `AssertionError: the fixture's bare remote must pin gc.autoDetach=false …
  got ''`
- `--no-hardlinks` removed -> `AssertionError: clone B shares 19 object file(s) with the
  remote by hardlink`

The second is also the direct measurement that the hardlink sharing was real, not inferred.

AC4: 20 consecutive runs of the file under CI's exact settings (`-n 4 --dist loadgroup`,
`--timeout=300`), each on a fresh basetemp, with `git fsck` run over every `remote.git` the
run produced. Result: 20/20 with 31 passed, zero test failures and zero corrupt remotes.

AC5: `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the full file passes (31 passed), as does the
reconciler unit tree (2409 passed).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
[operator-attested] EVIDENCE for AC4 and AC5. These two criteria are attested because their
proof is a local execution record, not a repository artifact.

LANDED: Gerrit change 1676, "Stop fixture remote rewriting itself mid-push", status MERGED
with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1. The Verified vote is CI's own execution of `make lint`,
`make typecheck` and the full suite against this patchset, so AC5 additionally has an
independent external witness beyond the local run below. Note for the record: patchset 1
took a Verified -1 that was NOT this change — the complexity-baseline lock reported a new
entry for `dispatch_one.py::_update_one_dispatch_links`, a function this test-only change
does not touch, introduced when main advanced. A rebase onto current main cleared it
(`check_complexity_baseline.py --check` then reported `active=60 new=0 increased=0
stale=0`). An earlier lint-job failure on the same patchset was an infrastructure flake: ruff
check and ruff format --check both passed, then the actionlint binary download returned HTTP
503 four times.

AC4 — command actually run, 20 iterations, each on a fresh basetemp that is deleted
afterwards, with `git fsck` run over every `remote.git` the iteration produced:

    for i in $(seq 1 20); do
      bt=/tmp/flakebase/run$i; rm -rf "$bt"
      python -m pytest tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py \
        -n 4 --dist loadgroup -q --timeout=300 --basetemp="$bt"
      for r in $(find "$bt" -name remote.git -maxdepth 4); do
        git --git-dir="$r" fsck --no-progress || echo "CORRUPT $r"
      done
    done

Result, one line per iteration, all 20 identical in shape:

    iter 1  rc=0 corruptremotes:none  31 passed in 35.36s
    …
    iter 20 rc=0 corruptremotes:none  31 passed in 34.24s
    TOTAL FAILS: 0 / 20

620 test executions, zero failures, and `git fsck` clean on every remote produced. Worth
recording because it shows the harness measured what it claims: an earlier run of the same
loop returned `TOTAL FAILS: 1 / 20`, and the single non-zero exit was the suite's own
repo-isolation guard reporting `REPO ISOLATION FAILURE … M tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/
orchestrate/test_reconcile_main.py` — an unrelated file this session was editing at the time
— with all 31 tests passing. Re-run against a clean tree, it was 0/20.

AC5 — `make lint` (ruff check, ruff format --check, complexity baseline, DCO identity,
criteria vocabulary, skill frontmatter, zizmor, actionlint) and `make typecheck` (mypy) both
pass locally on the committed tree:

    ruff check src tests scripts        -> All checks passed!
    ruff format --check src tests scripts -> 1929 files already formatted
    check_complexity_baseline --check   -> active=60 new=0 increased=0 stale=0
    mypy src/rebar scripts              -> Success: no issues found in 511 source files

Suite: the affected file passes (31 passed) and the reconciler unit tree passes (2409
passed). `make config-check` and `pre-commit run --all-files` also pass.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

`tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py::test_code_review_sidecar_emit_two_clone_union`
failed CI on the checked `git push origin HEAD:tickets` in `_assert_emit_is_append_only`
(currently line 1738), costing Gerrit change 1655 a spurious `Verified -1`.

## The filed premise is FALSIFIED (evidence in comments)

Filed hypothesis: a lost CAS / non-fast-forward between two clones racing the push leg. The
job's captured log disproves it. The push was rejected by the RECEIVING repository with
`unresolved deltas left after unpacking`, `remote unpack failed: unpack-objects abnormal
exit`, and `refs/heads/tickets does not point to a valid object!` — the remote rejected the
pack as an unpacker error. There is no `non-fast-forward`, no `cannot lock ref`, and no
OOM/signal anywhere in the job. The same warning repeats 18 times with a monotonically
climbing unpushed-commit counter, so the fixture's bare `remote.git` was already missing
objects from the FIRST emit push onward: the remote was corrupt before any assertion ran.

This is object loss inside the fixture's own remote, not a ref race between the two clones.
The earlier sibling occurrence failed differently (an empty clone-B event set, root-caused
and fixed by willing-cellular-carp), so the two are distinct mechanisms.

## Root cause

Three facts compose:

1. `two_clones` creates the bare remote with a plain `git init --bare` (line 216) and never
   configures it.
2. `_make_repo` clones that local path with no `--no-hardlinks` (line 66), so repo A/B
   `.git/objects` are HARDLINKED to `remote.git/objects`, and `.tickets-tracker` is a linked
   worktree sharing repo A's object database (`_commands/init.py:381`).
3. rebar's gc-config ensure unit (`_commands/init.py:112-155`) deliberately re-enables
   auto-gc but forces it FOREGROUND (`gc.autoDetach=false`, `maintenance.autoDetach=false`),
   precisely because a DETACHED background gc/maintenance repacking an object database
   outside the write lock corrupts the store (bug 88eb, ADR 0051; `_store/sync.py:17-26`).

That pinning reaches the tracker and its enclosing clone. It does NOT reach the bare remote.
`remote.git` is therefore the one repository in the fixture whose `receive-pack` runs
`git gc --auto` at git's defaults — DETACHED — after each of the ~50 emit pushes, repacking
and pruning its object store concurrently with the next incoming push. git-clone(1) also
warns that local hardlink clones can race with concurrent modification of the source
repository, which is exactly the shape here.

## Scope

Fixture/test-only; no `src/rebar` behaviour change. Fixing it at the remote-creation and
clone sites covers all 16 `push … HEAD:tickets` sites in this file at once.

Reconciled with depraved-frowzy-trout: that audit classified read-sync preconditions
(`_expire_sync_marker` to `_sync_from_origin`). It did not classify push sites, so there is
no kept-as-fail-fast decision being overturned here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1 — The fixture's bare remote is pinned to the same no-detached-upkeep posture rebar
      pins on trackers, and the clones no longer hardlink its object store. The reason is
      recorded at the fixture with the bug 88eb / ADR 0051 reference.
- [x] AC2 — A regression test asserts that posture on the fixture's remote, so a future
      fixture that drops the pin fails deterministically here rather than rarely in CI.
- [x] AC3 — Fail-fast preserved: a genuinely failing push still fails. Proven by a test that
      makes the remote reject a push and asserts the fixture's push path still raises. No
      retry, no swallowed error, and no wall-clock bound is introduced.
- [x] AC4 [operator-attested] — The affected file passes at least 20 consecutive runs under CI's settings
      (`-n 4 --dist loadgroup`), with the evidence recorded in a comment.
- [x] AC5 [operator-attested] — `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.
